Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photorealistic interior design reference for a newly completed residential entrance hall.
Primary request: rebuild the supplied simple computer-rendered room as a convincingly REAL built interior photographed by an architectural photographer, with a thoroughly redesigned finish package and genuinely manufactured doors, hardware, glazing, floor and light fixtures. This is a permitted full redesign of finishes and objects within the SAME room. It must not be a lightly retextured version of the primitive render.
Spatial invariants: use Image 1 as the exact spatial and camera template. Preserve camera position, image framing, perspective, room width/depth, all existing wall corners, ceiling height, floor boundary, locations/count/size of door openings and passage openings. Flat 3 m ceiling. No new structural walls, windows, niches, door openings or expanded spaces. Match the visible wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-floor intersections of Image 1 closely. The floor area cannot change. Secondary references must never dictate the room geometry.
Permitted design changes: freely replace the designs of existing door leaves, aluminium frames, handles, hinges, closers, glazing, floor finishes, skirting, wall panel composition, surface-mounted ceiling light fixtures and signage. Keep their architecture and operation believable. Build one coordinated design, not a material swatch pasted onto the existing cartoon.
Clean circulation: remove the existing stroller entirely if present and reconstruct the floor and wall behind it. No people, benches, consoles, chairs, plants, parcels, bicycles, new furniture, waiting area, movable decor or floor clutter. Keep the residential function and functional stroller-zone designation if present.
Photographic realism: real architectural photography of a finished new building, restrained full-frame lens perspective matching the reference, level verticals, tack-sharp real material response, fine paint stipple rather than perfectly plastic walls, restrained natural wood pores where requested, subtly different tile faces and tiny realistic joint shadows, professionally assembled metal profiles with visible glazing beads, seals, accurate hinges/handle mounts and soft real reflections. Clean new materials with subtle natural manufacturing variation, not dirt, damage or artificial ageing. No CGI sheen, smeared textures, vector-like objects, impossible reflections or oversized cartoon hardware.
Lighting: soft balanced architectural illumination, warm-white fixtures about 3000 K with neutral photographic white balance and lifted natural exposure. The room must be bright without white clipping or yellow/orange saturation. Fine metal-bodied linear surface-mounted ceiling luminaires, physically plausible diffuser and falloff, no dropped ceiling, no chandeliers, no dramatic hotel lighting, no overblown bloom or mirror floor.
Common residential character: quiet expensive appearance, light warm ivory/greige base, restrained graphite metal and satin accents. Matte or softly satin material finishes, understated stone pattern, readable circulation. Elevators, staircase and main entry identifiable; service doors quieter.
Text: only relevant existing functional labels, rendered accurately: "КОЛЯСОЧНАЯ" and stroller pictogram where present, "ЛЕСТНИЦА", "ЛИФТ →", "1", "ЭТАЖ" only when appropriate to the source view. Existing signage may be redesigned but must stay legible and logically associated with its function. No captions, extra labels, watermarks or fake logo/brand name in the image. No generic logo placeholder. Reserve a small calm unoccupied wall area for one future actual logo; do not write anything there.
Output: one full-frame landscape photograph-like image, approximately 3:2 like the source; one scene, no collage, no presentation board, no before/after.

Input images: Image 1 is the EXACT spatial edit target (existing hall). Image 2 is only a finish-detail/photographic-quality reference from Albina: borrow credible aluminium profiles, glass, timber grain, floor and fine hardware, but do not borrow its longer corridor, additional doors, mailboxes, windows or architecture.

BASELINE A1–A3, ONE COHERENT WOOD DESIGN.
Palette: warm ivory finely textured painted walls, medium neutral brown oak/walnut decor (strongly reduce orange), warm greige honed-look porcelain floor, slim dark graphite aluminium/metal details.
Wood accent: use the original wooden wall zones as the basis, but redesign the joinery as wide flat vertical panels with real timber grain and very narrow orderly shadow joints. For the stroller zone, replace the crude large gray lower slab with a much lower continuous approximately 150 mm warm greige stone skirting; wood reaches down to this skirting. Keep the original outer accent-wall boundaries. Do not carry the old 780 mm high protective slab into the new baseline.
Floor: calm matte warm greige stone-look porcelain, square approximately 600 mm modules, straight 2 mm joints, subtle face-to-face natural variation. Replace the chunky black perimeter border with a refined approximately 100–150 mm high matching stone skirting on the painted walls. No mirror shine.
Glazed doors: in the SAME openings use realistic slim graphite thermally profiled aluminium double doors, believable clear low-reflective glazing, fine seals, properly mounted slender cylindrical vertical pull handles of realistic diameter/length, actual hinges and discreet closers. Keep the source door count and existing relationship to the adjacent vestibule; do not invent additional rooms or outdoor scenes behind the glass.
Solid staircase door where present: medium neutral brown wood-faced standard single leaf with refined graphite frame, accurately proportioned lever handle, hinge line and discreet closer; upper wood panel may visually extend above the leaf within the original opening surround, but do not enlarge the opening.
Elevator where present: realistic satin dark graphite lift doors and matching head panel with slim warm medium-brown wood side panels in the original footprint; detailed flush call button with subtle indicator, crisp metal seams and clear floor numbering.
Fixtures: restrained fine-profile graphite linear ceiling luminaires. No gold in this baseline; calm and coherent.
Signage: dark graphite or understated light lettering for contrast with its immediate surface, correct spelling, slim professional lettering and small stroller symbol rather than the oversized crude wire icon. Leave the surrounding composition calm.
